title: Keel may deploy idle funds through discretionary GovOps approval until the Allocation System Primitive is implemented
content:
A.6.1.1.3.3.2 states that "In the short term prior to Keel's implementation of the Allocation System Primitive, Keel may invest idle funds in low-risk decentralized finance opportunities, including providing liquidity to established lending protocols on Solana. These deployments will be subject to the approval of Operational GovOps."

This is a bridge authority, and it substitutes one control regime for another. The Allocation System Primitive supplies structural control: a per-Instance Configuration Document, an on-chain Integration account holding rate limits, an Invocation process, and lifecycle branches recording success and failure. The interim regime supplies **discretionary** control instead: a human approval step by Operational GovOps.

Two qualifiers carry the weight. "Low-risk" is undefined and therefore judged case by case, and "established lending protocols on Solana" describes exactly the venues the Allocation System Primitive Instances also target — so the interim path and the Primitive path point at the same opportunities under different governance.

The tension with the surrounding Artifact is direct: the Primitive machinery exists precisely so that capital deployment does not depend on a discretionary approver, yet this provision authorises deployment on that basis. It is defensible as a transitional measure, and its own text bounds it by an event ("prior to Keel's implementation"). What it lacks is a deadline, a size cap, or a reporting requirement — none of the three appear — so the only thing terminating the interim regime is the arrival of the Primitive it is standing in for.
description: An interim authority permits low-risk DeFi deployments — including Solana lending protocols
